questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance Given the Number, Sum, and Sum of Squares of the Data Points
questions.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $8$ data points, where 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}=-56,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2}=560.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}=-56,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (-56) \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2}=560,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 560 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =70-{(-7)}^{2} \\  & =70-49 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
1,\,5,\,1,\,2,\,3,\,6,\,1,\,2,\,6
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=9$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (1+5+1+2+3+6+1+2+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot 27 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot ({1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (1+25+1+4+9+36+1+4+36) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot 117 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =13-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =13-9 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Standard Deviation of a Data Set
questions.problem:
Compute the standard deviation $\sigma $ of the following data set:

$$
15,\,1,\,-10,\,-13,\,-9
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (15+1-10-13-9) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-16) \\  & =-\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [{15}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-10)^{2}+(-13)^{2}+(-9)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [225+1+100+169+81] \\  & =\frac{576}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{576}{5}-{(-\frac{16}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{576}{5}-\frac{256}{25} \\  & =\frac{2880-256}{25} \\  & =\frac{2624}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2624}{25}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{41}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
-9,\,-5,\,3,\,8,\,-1,\,-4,\,-6
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (-9-5+3+8-1-4-6) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (-14) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot [(-9)^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}+{8}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-6)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot [81+25+9+64+1+16+36] \\  & =\frac{232}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{232}{7}-{(-2)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{232}{7}-4 \\  & =\frac{232-28}{7} \\  & =\frac{204}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{204}{7}} \\  & =2\sqrt{\frac{51}{7}}.\end{aligned}
$$
